candidate_v3_hypotheses.name: Collapse repeated candidate pairs around one short contact cluster
candidate_v3_hypotheses.physical_interpretation: Several generated source→target pairs can describe one rebound, shot or fragmented contact action.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.runtime_evidence: Existing pass candidate timestamps and consecutive-contact identifiers only.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.why_it_should_remove_false_positives: The audit finds repeated false-positive candidates within one documented diagnostic time cluster.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.genuine_pass_risk: Fast one-touch passing sequences can also be dense; preserve distinct player-to-player releases.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.measured_support: 35 false-positive candidates occur in multi-candidate diagnostic clusters; true clustered count not inferred as football truth (0).

candidate_v3_hypotheses.name: Trace same-player skip chains to a later distinct receiver before discarding a release
candidate_v3_hypotheses.physical_interpretation: The consecutive-contact builder can observe several contacts under one stable identity while a gold pass is anchored in the same sequence.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.runtime_evidence: Existing ordered contact IDs, stable-player IDs, skipped-pair reason and release trajectory evidence.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.why_it_should_remove_false_positives: This is a recall hypothesis rather than a false-positive filter: it targets a dominant documented construction loss without changing contact detection.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.genuine_pass_risk: Most same-player chains are continued control; any shadow rule must require a later distinct receiver and visible free-flight evidence.
candidate_v3_hypotheses.measured_support: 9 of 18 missed gold passes trace to a recorded same_player_consecutive_contacts skip.
